overview: The standard route and the only non-technical way up Baring Mountain: a brutally steep climbers' boot path up the west/northwest side to a talus basin, then a gully to the notch between the north and south summits and an easy class-3 ridge scramble to the top.
A 14-pitch, Grade V 5.11c line up a roughly 2,600-ft section of Baring's north face, established in September 1992.

Baring Mountain's North Face is one of the largest and most serious rock walls in the Cascades, rising roughly 3,000 feet above Barclay Lake. It is a committing, infrequently climbed alpine rock and mixed objective with significant loose rock and routefinding.

The peak's standard/easiest line: climbs the crest of Martin Peak's west ridge from Holden Pass to the summit, mostly Class 3 scrambling on loose schist with one short, well-featured Class 4 step just below the top.

A sustained six-pitch 5.8- alpine rock line up West McMillan Spire's southwest ridge, harder and more technical than the standard West Ridge scramble but sharing the same long approach via Terror Basin and the Terror Glacier.

A short, classic 5-pitch ridge route up Middle Gunsight's southwest side, starting with loose blocky climbing and finishing with enjoyable, easier climbing on cracks and knobs along an exposed ridge crest.

A 6-pitch, Grade III 5.10- moderate alpine rock route up the East Face of the smallest tower in the Liberty Bell Group, climbing progressively better rock to a stellar hand-crack finish near the summit.

Mount Adams's standard, non-technical route: a long snow slog up the broad southern flank via Crescent/Suksdorf Ridge, the Lunch Counter camp, and the false summit ('Piker's Peak') to the true summit beyond a shallow crater traverse.
